section: Government of India Act 1935 - provisions, provincial autonomy, 1937 elections and Congress ministries
subsections: Schedules and Lists - three lists, Governor's discretion

accepted.s: Under the Government of India Act, 1935, the Federal, Provincial and Concurrent Lists contained, respectively, how many subjects?
accepted.x: The Federal List contained 59 subjects, the Provincial List 54 subjects and the Concurrent List 36 subjects.
accepted.tq: Use the numerical association between the three lists and eliminate options that interchange their figures.
accepted.sec: Schedules and Lists - three lists, Governor's discretion

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the distribution of legislative subjects under the Government of India Act, 1935?
o: Provincial, Municipal and Concurrent Lists were provided
Federal, Provincial and Concurrent Lists were provided
Union, State and Local Lists were provided
Federal and Provincial Lists alone were provided
accepted.x: The Act divided subjects among Federal, Provincial and Concurrent Lists. The terminology Union, State and Local Lists belongs to a later constitutional framework.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the exact statutory terminology of the 1935 Act and familiar later constitutional terms.
accepted.sec: Schedules and Lists - three lists, Governor's discretion

accepted.s: In the absence of an entry in the Federal, Provincial or Concurrent List under the Government of India Act, 1935, residuary powers were vested in the
o: Federal Legislature
Provincial Governors
Secretary of State for India
Governor-General
accepted.x: The Government of India Act, 1935 assigned residuary powers to the Governor-General.
accepted.tq: Ask who would exercise the residual power and avoid confusing the Governor-General with provincial Governors.
accepted.sec: Schedules and Lists - three lists, Governor's discretion

accepted.s: Which of the following powers was associated with the Governor-General under the Government of India Act, 1935?
o: Suspending proceedings relating to a Bill and stopping discussion
Appointing all provincial ministers without legislative responsibility
Transferring all residuary powers to provincial legislatures
Abolishing the Concurrent List by executive order
accepted.x: The Governor-General could stop discussion and suspend proceedings relating to a Bill. The other alternatives do not describe the power mentioned in the Act.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ method to distinguish the Governor-General's power from provincial functions.
accepted.sec: Schedules and Lists - three lists, Governor's discretion

accepted.s: The Government of India Act, 1935 further extended the system of separate electorates to include which of the following groups?
o: Peasants, landlords and students
Workers, soldiers and civil servants only
Traders, zamindars and industrialists
Depressed classes, women and labour
accepted.x: The separate electorate system was extended further to depressed classes, women and labour.
accepted.tq: Test the exact membership of a statutory category through a closely related group-list option.
accepted.sec: Schedules and Lists - three lists, Governor's discretion

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT a measure undertaken by the Congress ministries in the sphere of civil liberties?
o: Releasing political prisoners
Restoring press freedom
Lifting emergency powers
Imposing wider bans on leftist organisations
accepted.x: Congress ministries lifted bans on leftist bodies; they did not impose wider bans on them. They also lifted emergency powers, released political prisoners and restored press freedom.
accepted.tq: Find the reversed policy among a cluster of civil-liberties measures.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the civil-liberties record of the Congress ministries:
1. Emergency powers were lifted.
2. Political prisoners were released.
3. Press freedom was restored.
4. Bans on leftist bodies were lifted.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: All four measures formed part of the civil-liberties record of the Congress ministries: emergency powers were lifted, prisoners released, bans on leftist bodies removed and press freedom restored.
accepted.tq: Check whether all listed measures belong to the same policy cluster before selecting the complete combination.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the agrarian measures of the Congress ministries?
o: Tenancy Acts — protection of tenancy interests
Begar — compulsory continuation of forced labour
Debt relief — withdrawal of relief from indebted peasants
Agrarian policy — abolition of all provincial legislatures
accepted.x: Tenancy Acts, including measures in the United Provinces, were part of the agrarian legislative record. The Congress ministries also worked towards abolition of begar and debt relief.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair and reject options that reverse the meaning of a reform.

accepted.s: The abolition of begar by the Congress ministries was primarily related to the removal of
o: separate electorates
industrial disputes
forced labour
press restrictions
accepted.x: Begar referred to forced or compulsory labour, and its abolition was an agrarian and social measure of the Congress ministries.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely related reform terms by identifying the exact practice to which each refers.

accepted.s: The Industrial Disputes Act associated with the legislative record of the Congress ministries was enacted in
accepted.x: The Industrial Disputes Act referred to in this context was enacted in 1938 and formed part of the labour measures of the Congress ministries.
accepted.tq: Use the year-specific legislative fact and distinguish it from the years of the Act, elections and resignations.

accepted.s: Which of the following measures best reflects the labour policy of the Congress ministries?
o: Extension of begar to industrial establishments
Recognition of trade-union rights and enactment of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1938
Abolition of all trade unions and suspension of industrial legislation
Transfer of labour legislation exclusively to the Governor-General
accepted.x: The Congress ministries promoted trade-union rights and enacted the Industrial Disputes Act in 1938. The other alternatives contradict the stated labour record.
accepted.tq: Match the policy objective with the specific labour legislation and institutional reform associated with it.

accepted.s: Which one of the following was an important measure adopted for the upliftment of Harijans by the Congress ministries?
o: Free education
Compulsory separate electorates for all communities
Restriction of access to public education
Abolition of provincial legislatures
accepted.x: Free education and other upliftment measures for Harijans formed part of the social-welfare programme of the Congress ministries.
accepted.tq: Identify the positive welfare measure among options that reverse or obstruct social reform.

accepted.s: The Government of India Act, 1935 is often regarded as a blueprint of the Constitution of India because
o: large parts of the constitutional structure were derived from it
it introduced universal adult franchise throughout India
it abolished all forms of provincial government
it established the Constitution of India in its final form
accepted.x: The Act is regarded as a blueprint because large parts of the structure of the Constitution of India were derived from its institutional framework. It did not itself establish the later Constitution or universal adult franchise.
accepted.tq: Reject the extreme claims and select the precise structural comparison.

accepted.s: The present relevance of Section 63 of the Government of India Act, 1935 is most directly seen in debates concerning
o: Governors' addresses in Opposition-ruled States, along with Article 175
the composition of the Union Public Service Commission under Article 315
the appointment of the Election Commission under Article 324
the financial emergency under Article 360
accepted.x: Contemporary rows concerning Governors' addresses in Opposition-ruled States are traced to Section 63 of the 1935 Act and Article 175 of the Constitution.
accepted.tq: Link the historical provision with its modern constitutional parallel rather than with an unrelated constitutional power.

accepted.s: The provincial autonomy introduced under the Government of India Act, 1935 had a particular significance for Andhra because it
o: immediately created a separate Andhra State in 1937
ended the Coastal-Rayalaseema regional question permanently
abolished the Madras Presidency before the 1937 elections
made the prospect of an Andhra State appear achievable
accepted.x: Provincial autonomy made the objective of an Andhra State appear achievable. It did not immediately create such a State or abolish the Madras Presidency.
accepted.tq: Distinguish between creating a political possibility and actually implementing the final territorial demand.

accepted.s: What had to be addressed before the 1937 provincial elections in the Andhra context?
o: The division of the Federal List into two lists
The abolition of the Concurrent List
The dispute over the Governor-General's residuary powers
The Coastal-Rayalaseema rift
accepted.x: The Coastal-Rayalaseema rift had to be closed before the 1937 elections in order to consolidate the Andhra position.
accepted.tq: Identify the regional political issue connected with the election context instead of confusing it with constitutional lists.

accepted.s: The Sri Bagh Pact of 1937 was associated with the effort to close the
o: Congress–Justice Party coalition dispute
Federal–Provincial legislative dispute
Coastal-Rayalaseema rift
Governor–Governor-General jurisdictional dispute
accepted.x: The Sri Bagh Pact of 1937 was associated with resolving the Coastal-Rayalaseema rift in the Andhra context.
accepted.tq: Use the regional association of the pact to eliminate constitutionally unrelated disputes.

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Sri Bagh Pact
(b) Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao
(c) Sreerbagh
(d) 1937

List-II
(i) Year of the pact
(ii) House associated with the pact
(iii) Person whose house hosted the pact
(iv) Name associated with the pact's venue

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
o: a–i, b–iii, c–iv, d–ii
a–i, b–iii, c–ii, d–iv
a–ii, b–iv, c–iii, d–i
a–iv, b–ii, c–i, d–iii
accepted.x: The Sri Bagh Pact was concluded in 1937 at the house of Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao. The house was called Sreerbagh, giving the pact its associated name.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure year and person pairs, then distinguish the venue from the name of the pact.

accepted.s: Which statement correctly describes the first Congress government in the Madras Presidency?
o: It was formed in 1937 under the Justice Party and ended provincial autonomy.
It was formed in 1939 under Rajaji and ended the system of separate electorates.
It was formed in 1937 under Rajaji and ended Justice Party rule that had lasted from 1920 to 1937.
It was formed in 1935 under Rajaji and ended Congress rule in the Presidency.
accepted.x: The first Congress government in Madras was formed in 1937 under Rajaji, bringing to an end Justice Party rule from 1920 to 1937.
accepted.tq: Combine the distinctive first, year, leader and preceding party rule while rejecting swapped dates and parties.
